# BOOK 1 OF 2: THE DATCHET DIAMONDS (Richard Marsh; Gutenberg 40353; illustrated by Stanley L. Wood; frontispiece "Shall I shoot all three of you?" p.265)

## Chapters
I Two Men and a Maid; II Overheard in the Train; III The Diamonds; IV Miss Wentworth's Rudeness; V In the Bodega; VI The Adventures of a Night; VII The Datchet Diamonds Are Placed in Safe Custody; VIII In the Moment of His Success; IX A Proposal of Marriage; X Cyril's Friend; XI John Ireland's Warrant; XII A Woman Roused; XIII The Detective and the Lady; XIV Among Thieves; XV Put to the Question; XVI A Modern Instance of an Ancient Practice; XVII The Most Dangerous Foe of All; XVIII The Last of the Datchet Diamonds; XIX A Woman's Logic

## Characters
- **Daisy (Miss Daisy) Strong**: young woman, lives Medina Villas, Brighton, with friend Charlie; mother died; £120/yr from mother; engaged to Cyril.
- **Cyril Paxton**: City speculator/stockbroker, gambler; lost on "Eries" (shares), bought 10,000 Trumpit Gold Mine shares (worthless until boom: later £10–£12 10s each); has Gladstone bag; pockets a quarter-million-pound diamond haul by mistake.
- **Charlotte "Charlie" Wentworth**: 30, journalist/writer (Fashion pages), wears pince-nez, sharp-tongued; Daisy's friend and housemate.
- **Mr. Lawrence** (alias of Reginald Hargraves, "The Toff"): blue eyes, soft voice, pink-and-white complexion; met Daisy on Devil's Dyke via umbrella in rain; proposes to Daisy; thief.
- **The German-American / "Baron"** (alias Isaac Bergstein): tall, thin, stoop, long black overcoat, huge top hat, hollow cheeks, clawlike finger, nasal accent, vulture-like nose.
- **Stephen Eversleigh**: duchess's manservant, short-sighted, spectacles gift from duke; swapped despatch-box trick.
- **John Ireland**: Scotland Yard detective (Inspector, CID); bets Franklyn £100 at evens that Paxton has guilty knowledge.
- **Mr. Franklyn**: lawyer (solicitor), Cyril's friend, holds 10,000 Trumpit shares in strongbox; about 40, grey-streaked hair.
- **Hollier**: policeman set to follow Franklyn.
- **Bill Cooper**: undersized shabby informer ("Bill"), 10 "thick 'uns"/£50 from Daisy.
- **Tom the Toff** (= Lawrence) and **the Baron** named by Cooper.
- **Skittles**: henchman with pail (Lord Mayor and Aldermen joke); burned by iron, struck by Paxton.
- **Treadwater**: Makell's Hotel manager; clerk with curled moustache.
- **Duchess of Datchet**; Duke of Datchet; Bartlett's Bank; Grosvenor Square mansion; Amsterdam Necklace (~£100,000); Datchet Tiara; Begum's Brooch; Banee's Bracelet.

## Plot events in order
1. Brighton pier, April. Daisy with Lawrence (acquaintance began on Devil's Dyke in rain, umbrella). Cyril appears; "Where's Charlie?" Quarrel: Cyril says he's "going for the gloves" (bull on Eries), will win or lose "by this time tomorrow." Daisy: if he loses, relations end; "We must be as strangers." Daisy kisses Cyril.
2. Train to London: news of Duchess of Datchet's diamonds robbery (£250,000; despatch-box; left Windsor 4:05 train, Paddington, Grosvenor Sq; empty on opening at Bartlett's agent). Cyril overhears through pivoting glass panel Lawrence and German-American in next compartment: Eversleigh's spectacle case duplicated (photo by friend), exchange at Windsor booking office; Eversleigh's despatch-box swapped with rug-covered duplicate; Lawrence took it by South-Western line. Cyril's train via Preston Park.
3. Brighton Central refreshment room: Lawrence offers drink; Cyril leaves. In Makell's Hotel bedroom Cyril finds Lawrence's Gladstone (identical brown new bag) with diamonds: a ring, tiara, necklace, etc., hidden in shirts. Stuffs gems in evening paper.
4. Cyril meets Daisy on pier; tells her of "fortune" (quarter million); she proposes marriage within a month; Charlie hostile; Cyril storms out.
5. Bodega: Lawrence and German-American ask "what was the colour of your Gladstone bag?" Cyril denies. John Ireland appears; hints he knows where diamonds are; says lifer for possessor.
6. Shadowed through Brighton; Cyril lodges Gladstone in hotel safe. Night: intruder with ladder at window; Cyril shoots at him (revolver under pillow).
7. Morning: Cyril takes diamonds to Chancery Lane Deposit Company safe; ruse at station (man in billycock, fake fall at London Bridge).
8. Returns to Brighton; bag claimed by shabby man ("Medina Villas"); Trumpit shares boom to £10; Cyril had bought 10,000 shares earlier. Kidnapped by chloroform outside Makell's Hotel.
9. Daisy waits on pier; Lawrence proposes to her (says Cyril stays in town). Daisy sends Franklyn news; Franklyn (Cyril's lawyer) reveals shares at £12 10s. Franklyn goes to hotel, meets Ireland, who reveals warrant for Paxton and ring found on Paxton; Ireland bets £100 and sets Hollier to follow Franklyn.
10. Daisy and Charlie at Makell's; Ireland searches bag; Daisy defends Cyril. Cooper reveals Tom the Toff and the Baron have Paxton captive.
11. Cyril in chloroform-stupor, bound, tortured by Skittles (pail) and the Baron (revolver, "singe lobe of left ear"); Lawrence proposes; branding iron with "thief" on Cyril's shoulder-blade; Cyril frees hands, knocks out Baron and Lawrence, lamp smashed; fire; Cyril locked in pantry cupboard; writes will "to my dear love, Daisy Strong."
12. Police (Ireland, Cooper) find house burning; Daisy rescues Cyril from window. Trial: Lawrence (Hargraves) and Baron (Bergstein) get twenty years' penal servitude.
13. Epilogue: Cyril sells shares, consols; marries Daisy quietly in Brighton church. Daisy's logic about the pier; Cyril's prayer.

# BOOK 2 OF 2: A DEAD RECKONING (T. W. Speight; Gutenberg 57737; Chambers's Journal, 14 Sept 1889; 19 chapters)

## Characters
- **Clara Brooke** (née Danby; 22, charming brunette, black eyes, olive complexion). Husband **Gerald Brooke** (26, tall, fair, reddish-brown hair, dark blue laughing eyes; Polish-raised; owner of Beechley Towers, 14 miles from London; shooting skill). 
- **Aunt Jane Primby**: fresh-coloured spinster, secret age, embroidery, nerves; loves "Count de Bonnechose" story, Major Pondicherry, Dean of Rathdrum, Mr. Tubbins brewer.
- **Lady Fanny ("Lady Fan") Dwyer**: friend; husband **Algy** (yacht, Mediterranean); married 18 months+; her maid Simpkins; Sir William's horses; Seaton Park.
- **Baron Otto von Rosenberg**: ex-German diplomat, carefully preserved, ~40–55, iron-grey hair; took Beaulieu lease; borrowed Gerald's gold-and-ivory Indian pistol.
- **George Crofton**: Gerald's cousin, dark, sallow, thin, gash in upper lip with tooth showing; disinherited; loved Clara; mistress Stephanie Lagrange (circus "Queen of the Haute Ecole," later Mrs. Crofton).
- **Karovsky (M. Paul Karovsky)**: Russian, tall, yellow-ivory complexion, black hair parted middle; secret Society ("Supreme Tribunal"); delivers death sentence on Von Rosenberg to Gerald, who refuses; "Remember!".
- **Henri Picot** (boy, 8–9, golden curls, fillet, mother Marie dead) and **Jules Picot** (mountebank, "Monsieur Picot," drum and Pandean pipes; original name tied to Stephanie as daughter).
- **Stephanie Lagrange** = Picot's daughter (Stephanie Picot).
- **Margery Shook**: 16–17, orphan, ex-canal-barge girl, nut-brown hair, odd witch-laugh, dialect; saved by Clara; devoted.
- **Bunce**: pompous butler/majordomo. **Dixon**: groom. **Drumley**: superintendent of police, King's Harold. **Tom Starkie**: red-haired friend; father **Sir John Starkie** JP of Penrhyn Court. **Roger Chamfrey**: friend, moor in Yorkshire; keeper **Timley**. **Pedley**: discharged groom who stole the half-burnt letter.
- **Slinkey** and **"Lardy Bill"** (sham clergyman, later "Colonel Crofton" in jail); **Dr. King**; **Mr. Pringle** (baron's man); **Mrs. Purvis** (landlady of Beechley Arms); **Lucas** (Gerald's mate at signal box).

## Plot events in order
1. April 24. Clara, Aunt Jane, Lady Fan at Beechley Towers. Clara married 6 months to Gerald. Lady Fan explains her "modus vivendi" (married people should live apart). Baron Von Rosenberg and Gerald practise pistols. Picot (mountebank, son Henri) brought before Clara; Clara gives Henri cakes and money. Picot startled at Von Rosenberg's name.
2. Gerald and Baron walk to Beaulieu; Gerald gives Baron the Indian pistol. George Crofton visits Clara, expresses bitter love, leaves. He crushes Gerald's miniature on hearth; wishes Gerald dead; inheritance (Beechley Towers + £6,000 a year) would pass to him if Gerald dies without heirs.
3. Crofton with Stephanie at Beechley Arms; Stephanie meets Henri; learns her mother and sister story. Stephanie learns Clara was Crofton's old love (Clara Danby).
4. Karovsky visits Gerald: Gerald (member of secret Society since age 18 in Warsaw) ordered to assassinate Von Rosenberg, who betrayed Society in St. Petersburg; Karovsky's brother died in mines. Gerald refuses; Karovsky: "Remember!"
5. Ten weeks later (late June): Gerald's letter warning Baron unfinished, burnt. Baron found shot dead at Beaulieu chalet ~7pm 28 June. Clara and aunt learn it. Gerald's pistol found near body. Margery warns; police warrant. Gerald hides in Penrhyn Court's "Priest's Hole" with Tom's help. Clara and Gerald plan; Clara lies to Drumley; Gerald escapes via panel; house searched.
6. Gerald hides in Penrhyn Court; then as "Davis" keeper on Yorkshire moor (Timley); disguise black hair dye. Clara and aunt move to London, 5 Pymm's Buildings, Soho, as "Mr. and Mrs. Stewart." Picot lodges top floor.
7. Karovsky visits, offers funds; Gerald refuses. Police arrive; Karovsky impersonates Gerald and is taken (sergeant). Crofton reveals he informed police; Picot gags and binds Crofton; Crofton escapes by burning ropes.
8. Crofton and Stephanie: Crofton plans robbery of jewellery box bound for Lord Leamington's seat (April 14 journey, Cummerhays line). Stephanie refuses.
9. Lady Fan visits Clara at Cinder Pit Junction signal box (Gerald works as signalman under name Maynard; Mrs. Maynard). Lady Fan offers Algy's bank; Gerald refuses. Margery reveals Crofton's gang plans attack at Cinder Pit Junction; Clara and Margery overhear.
10. Clara creeps to signal box; Gerald has been bound to tree by Lardy Bill and Slinkey; Clara frees him. Crofton's gang meet train; fog-signals stop train; Margery warns driver. Gang surrounded; Crofton shoots Gerald (wounded arm); Crofton denounced Gerald as murderer.
11. Cummerhays court: Picot confesses to killing Von Rosenberg (he shot him after Baron refused info about his daughter Stephanie, who fled with Baron). Picot found dead in cell from poison phial in heel. Crofton escapes from jail with help of "Colonel Crofton" (Lardy Bill). Stephanie learns father confession, reads Picot's letter (Henri died in winter; Picot's letter to "Madame Brouke"). 
12. Final: six weeks later Gerald returns to Beechley Towers; Lady Fan, Tom Starkie, Miss Primby, Margery present. Crofton shoots at Gerald from window; dark-cloaked figure (Karovsky's Brotherhood) disarms him; Crofton dies. Karovsky: sentence "carried into effect"; Gerald absolved. END.
